bugs.name: Heartbeat history table lists only one of five checks
bugs.summary: The monitor label says “Heartbeat history: 5 checks, 5 up, 0 down” and the chart plots five samples, but the table contains only one row: “Up 2026-10-08 14:33:53 200 - OK”.
bugs.expected: The history table should expose the heartbeat records represented by the monitor's five-check history, or indicate that only a subset is displayed.
bugs.actual: The monitor label says “Heartbeat history: 5 checks, 5 up, 0 down” and the chart plots five samples, but the table contains only one row: “Up 2026-10-08 14:33:53 200 - OK”.
reproSteps: Open /dashboard/2
Open the Dashboard.
Open the non-first monitor “Application Entry API”.
Inspect its 24-hour heartbeat chart and the history table below it.
bugs.reason: Details explicitly loads important-heartbeat history and shows a No important events state. Repeated healthy checks belong in full history/chart but need not add rows to this event table.

bugs.name: IP Family helper text omits the algorithm name
bugs.summary: The helper reads “Uses the for determining the IP family.” and the “Happy Eyeballs algorithm” link appears separately afterward.
bugs.expected: The IP Family helper should state what it uses to determine the IP family, including the linked Happy Eyeballs algorithm name.
bugs.actual: The helper reads “Uses the for determining the IP family.” and the “Happy Eyeballs algorithm” link appears separately afterward.
reproSteps: Open /edit/2
Open the Dashboard.
Open the non-first Application Entry API monitor.
Select Edit and inspect Advanced > IP Family.
bugs.reason: The translation contains a happyEyeballs placeholder and the i18n-t component supplies the algorithm link in that named inline slot. Split extracted text does not establish missing visible text. If a screenshot genuinely shows reordered/missing text, reopen as a rendering bug.

bugs.name: Saving a blank clone name creates an uptime-kuma monitor
bugs.summary: After clearing Friendly Name, the form showed the placeholder “uptime-kuma”; Save created a new monitor named “uptime-kuma” (#6) using the source monitor URL.
bugs.expected: The clone form should block submission without a Friendly Name or require a valid name rather than creating a generic monitor.
bugs.actual: After clearing Friendly Name, the form showed the placeholder “uptime-kuma”; Save created a new monitor named “uptime-kuma” (#6) using the source monitor URL.
reproSteps: Open /dashboard/6
Open the non-first Application Entry API monitor.
Choose Clone.
Clear the Friendly Name field.
Select Save.
bugs.reason: Save deliberately substitutes defaultFriendlyName when the name is blank; HTTP monitor default names derive from their host. This is the expected clone/default-name behavior.

bugs.name: gRPC service and method labels focus the Proto Content field
bugs.summary: The gRPC monitor's Proto Service Name and Proto Method labels both focus the protobuf body instead of their respective inputs. Typing after clicking either label changes Proto Content while leaving the intended value empty.
bugs.expected: Clicking each label focuses its service-name or method input so typing populates that value.
bugs.actual: Both labels focus the Proto Content textarea. The typed text changes Proto Content and the service/method field remains empty; reproduced through visible label clicks and keyboard typing.
reproSteps: Sign in, open Add New Monitor, and select gRPC(s) - Keyword.
Click the Proto Service Name label, then type ServiceLabelTest.
Observe which field received the text.
Repeat by clicking the Proto Method label and typing a method name.
bugs.reason: The report is about labels moving focus to another input and typing after that focus movement. No supplied requirements/documentation promise label focus behavior. The explicit rule excludes focus movement even when surprising; choose not_a_bug without independently assigned, non-focus task failure.

bugs.name: MQTT WebSocket Path label does not focus its input
bugs.summary: The MQTT WebSocket Path label has no associated input target. Clicking it leaves focus on the page body, so subsequent typing does not fill the path field.
bugs.expected: Clicking the label focuses the adjacent path input and keyboard typing fills it.
bugs.actual: Focus remains on BODY and the path field stays unchanged. The label points to mqttWebsocketPath, but the visible path textbox has no corresponding ID.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Add New Monitor.
Select MQTT and locate the MQTT WebSocket Path input.
Click the MQTT WebSocket Path label.
Type a path using the keyboard.
bugs.reason: The visible field stays unchanged because clicking its label does not focus it; the ID mismatch is markup explanation. Focus behavior and missing IDs are categorically excluded without explicit requirements. There is no independently verified non-accessibility product failure.

bugs.name: HTTP Authentication Method label changes the HTTP request method
bugs.summary: The Method label beneath Authentication focuses the separate request-method dropdown under HTTP Options. Keyboard selection after clicking it changes GET/POST/etc. while authentication remains None.
bugs.expected: The Authentication Method label focuses its own authentication dropdown so keyboard selection chooses an authentication scheme.
bugs.actual: It focuses the HTTP request-method dropdown. On a fresh form, ArrowDown/Enter changed HTTP GET to POST while Authentication remained None. Independently reproduced in Edit changing POST to PUT; no unintended changes were saved.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Add New Monitor with HTTP(s) selected.
Under Authentication, click its Method label.
Press ArrowDown then Enter to select a method.
Inspect both the HTTP Options Method and Authentication Method dropdowns.
bugs.reason: Clicking Authentication Method moves focus to HTTP method, and arrow-key selection changes that focused control. The finding is explicitly a label/focus issue with no supplied focus contract. General label conventions do not override the rule's not_a_bug requirement.

bugs.name: gRPC service and method labels focus Proto Content instead of their fields
bugs.summary: The gRPC monitor editor associates Proto Service Name and Proto Method labels with the Proto Content textarea, so clicking the labels sends typing to the wrong field.
bugs.expected: Each label focuses its corresponding service-name or method input.
bugs.actual: Both labels focus the Proto Content textarea. Both labels reference id protobuf, while the actual service and method inputs have duplicate id name. Reproduced on the editor.
reproSteps: Sign in and add or edit a gRPC(s) - Keyword monitor.
Click the visible Proto Service Name label.
Observe which field receives focus.
Click the Proto Method label and observe focus again.
bugs.reason: Both service/method labels focus Proto Content, justified by duplicate/misassigned IDs. Focus movement and implementation label association are explicitly excluded without a supplied requirement. There is no independently assigned ordinary field-editing failure; not_a_bug.

bugs.name: RabbitMQ Management Nodes control replaces first URL when a second is entered
bugs.summary: Entering a second RabbitMQ Management Nodes URL replaces the first URL in the visible list, so the control cannot retain both configured nodes.
bugs.expected: After pressing Enter for the second URL, both the primary and secondary URLs should remain listed in the RabbitMQ Management Nodes control. The label and placeholder identify this as a list of management nodes.
bugs.actual: After entering the secondary URL and pressing Enter, the control displayed only http://rabbitmq-secondary.invalid:15672; the primary URL was gone. This remained visible after waiting and was reproduced again from a refreshed form with a fresh monitor name.
reproSteps: Open /add using the supplied saved session for the authorized administrator; authentication details were not changed.
Select RabbitMQ as the monitor type.
Enter the fresh friendly name mc-proto-msg-rabbit-20260619-9f3c.
In RabbitMQ Management Nodes, enter http://rabbitmq-primary.invalid:15672 and press Enter.
In the same control, enter http://rabbitmq-secondary.invalid:15672 and press Enter.
Inspect the control before saving: only the secondary URL is listed. Refresh /add, repeat with a new mc-proto-msg-rabbit-* name, and confirm the same result.
bugs.reason: Both primary and secondary RabbitMQ management URLs remain visible after their Enter actions, including after repeating on a refreshed form. The reported replacement of the first URL does not occur.
